name: Primer - Printed How-To-Play Spread from Your Input Bindings
summary: Composes a printed how-to-play booklet spread from your game's own input bindings and tutorial steps. Rebind a key and the diagram, callouts and legend redraw.
description:
The printed how-to-play page, composed from your game's own input bindings and tutorial steps. It redraws when a key is rebound.

Primer draws a saddle-stitched instruction booklet spread: two facing pages of cream stock, printed in two spot inks. FIG. 1 on the left is your active control scheme drawn whole, every bound control tethered by a numbered callout to a legend. The right page is your numbered steps, each with its screenshot re-screened as a two-ink halftone, and a hazard key. The result is an ordinary Texture2D for uGUI, UI Toolkit or a material.

Rebind Jump from Space to the south face button at runtime and the diagram, the callout numbering, the leader and the legend row all move, because all four are derived from the same list. That is the difference between this and a sheet of input icons.

78 HAND-AUTHORED MARKS

Keyboard: 7 cap forms and 14 special keys, each with a drawn legend.
Gamepad: face buttons by position, the D-pad and its four directions, left and right sticks as separate drawings with press and four pushes each, shoulders, triggers and system buttons.
Mouse and touch: 10 mouse marks including the thumb buttons, and 6 touch gestures.
Page furniture: the callout disc, leader terminals, figure frames, the hazard triangle, six hazard icons and the saddle-stitch staple.
Every control mark has a pressed state that is a different drawing, not a tint.

THREE WEIGHTS, BECAUSE THERE ARE THREE STATES

A bound key prints at full ink with a numbered callout. A key your game never mentions is ghosted, so the board still reads as a board. A control your game lists but leaves unbound gets an outlined cap and its own legend row reading "Dash (unbound)", so a player learns the action exists and has no key yet.

A REAL PRINT JOB

Four paper stocks (cream, newsprint, bright, kraft) decide the paper, the ink, the halftone dot pitch and the ink spread. Screenshots are separated into two plates and halftoned at 15 and 75 degrees, with levels read off your own image. The page count is derived from your steps, so there is no page-count field to maintain. The same book composes to the same pixels every time.

WORKS WITH ANY INPUT SETUP

A control is the generic Input System path, exactly the string InputBinding.effectivePath gives you. The composing code has no dependency on the Input System package, so it works the same on the legacy Input Manager, Rewired, or your own bindings file. Controls are drawn by position, never as a console manufacturer's trademarked glyph.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Primer/.
2. Open Demo/Scenes/PrimerDemo.unity and press Play. Left and right page through three sample games; press R to rebind a control and watch the page redraw.
3. Open Window > CSAF > Primer to see the same thing in the Editor, with a derivation panel that explains every choice the composer made.
4. In your own scene, add the CSAF/Primer/Primer Page component, assign the three typefaces from Assets/CSAF/Primer/Typefaces, give it a PrimerBook (a title, a list of controls, a list of steps, optional hazards) and call Rebuild() from your own rebinding callback.
technical:
Features: two-page printed instruction spread generated from your own input bindings and tutorial steps; 78 hand-authored marks across keyboard, gamepad, mouse, touch and page furniture, each control with a distinct pressed drawing; bound, ghosted and listed-but-unbound weights; numbered callouts with a leader router; four paper stocks; two-ink halftone of your screenshots; derived page count; hazard key; included TrueType outline reader; PrimerPage component with a Rebuild API; thread-safe compose path; deterministic output.

Number of C# scripts: 28 (25 Runtime, 2 Editor, 1 Demo). Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Primer.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Primer.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Primer.Demo (demo scene script).
Editor window: Window > CSAF > Primer. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Primer/Demo/Scenes/PrimerDemo.unity.
Minimum Unity version: 2022.3. Built and tested against 6000.5.7f1.
Render pipelines: Built-In, URP and HDRP. The page is rasterised into a Texture2D on the CPU and never touches the render pipeline.
Dependencies: none. The composing code takes generic control path strings and does not depend on the Input System package. No Resources folder, no network calls, no telemetry.
Asset uses Barlow Condensed, IBM Plex Mono and Source Sans 3 under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; see Third-Party Notices.txt in the package for details.

Documentation: https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/primer/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the software rasteriser, the TrueType outline reader, the mark corpus, the binding and step model, the halftone screen, the layout and callout router, the editor window and the demo scene.

The pages the package produces are not made by an image model. Every mark is drawn by the shipped code from authored geometry, offline and deterministically, with lettering filled from the outlines of the three shipped fonts. Those typefaces are third-party fonts by their own authors, shipped under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The store images are captures and composites of the package's output. Some of them, including the cover, set that output over an AI-generated illustrated background.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
